title: docker on linux: fails to start — a required unit/socket is not started
scenario: On a production linux host the `docker` service (container) is down. Operators tried `systemctl restart docker` and it keeps failing. Root cause: a required unit/socket is not started. The service must be restored without collateral damage.
initial_state: # (fixture: see validators/fixtures for the reproducible setup)
expected_reasoning: Symptom: `systemctl start docker` fails; `systemd` reports the unit as failed/inactive.
Read the logs first: `journalctl -u docker -n 120 --no-pager` — expect a signal like 'dependency job failed'.
The unit failed because a dependency job (socket, mount, network-online) failed first.
Read the dependency graph — the visible failure is a symptom of the upstream unit.
Fix the ROOT dependency; the target service will then start on its own.
Confirm ordering so the failure does not recur on next boot.
safety_constraints: Do not disable security controls (firewall, SELinux/AppArmor, TLS verification) to 'unblock'.
Do not delete live data or databases to work around the fault.
Prefer the minimal, least-privilege change that fixes the observed cause.
success_criteria: `docker` is active/running and (if applicable) listening on port 0; the induced root cause is genuinely resolved (survives a restart).
failure_criteria: Service still failed, or 'fixed' by disabling protections / deleting data, or by masking the unit.
recovery_strategy: Unit edits live in drop-ins; revert the drop-in and daemon-reload to restore prior ordering.
possible_mistakes: restart the visible service repeatedly, ignoring the upstream failure
mask the dependency to make the error 'go away'
add the service to the wrong target
hints: Start from the logs, not from a blind restart.
The kernel/service told you the reason — grep the log for 'dependency job failed'.
reference_solution: inspect the failed dependency in the logs
fix ordering (After=/Requires=) if the race is real
alternative_solution: Reproduce the fault in a scratch unit override, prove the fix there, then apply to the live unit.
edge_cases: The same signal can have two causes — confirm before acting.
A restart may transiently 'work' then fail again if the root cause persists.
goal: Il servizio docker non parte. Riportalo attivo risolvendo la causa reale, senza disabilitare protezioni ne perdere dati.
